n.story:
In the coming years, your role will face significant pressure from industrial automation, but a path remains for those who transition from manual labor to technical oversight. The repetitive, physically demanding tasks—filling moulds, removing excess mixture, and extracting products—are increasingly handled by robotic arms and automated systems that don't tire. Your workday will shift from the physical strain of the moulding floor to the precision of the control room.

You will become a 'craft-technician.' While sensors monitor the drying process and clay burning levels, you will use your deep, tactile knowledge of pottery materials to calibrate these systems. You will step in when the AI detects an anomaly that requires human intuition, such as a subtle change in clay consistency that a sensor might misinterpret. Your value lies in maintaining the quality standards and 'soul' of the product that machines cannot yet replicate, overseeing a fleet of automated tools to ensure every brick meets artisanal standards.

amp: Precision quality control and defect analysis

n.story:
Your role is transitioning from a manual machine operator to a high-tech production specialist. While the core of your craft remains rooted in the physical behavior of clay, the 'guesswork' of the factory floor is disappearing. AI-driven sensors now handle the repetitive monitoring of jigger machines and pug mills, while computer vision systems perform quality inspections with a level of precision that far exceeds the human eye, instantly flagging microscopic cracks or thickness inconsistencies.
